newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business news - May 13.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business news - May 13.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In a result which forced building materials giant CSR Ltd to slash its final dividend by 40 per cent to nine cents a share, only partly franked, the blue-chip group posted a 36 per cent drop in annual net profit yesterday to A$212.2 million, on sales of A6.1 billion. The result was the company's worst profit in over 10 years. Page 1.

In a speech to the Australian Telecommunications Users Group's annual general conference in Sydney today, Australian Competition and Consumer Commission chairman Allan Fels will warn that the Commission will take a strict stand against anti-competitive behaviour, and will effectively warn industry giant Telstra not to exploit its market power. Page 1.

In a deal valued at close to A$120 million, the Michigan-based utility group CMS Energy Corporation won a bidding duel yesterday for the West Australian Natural Gas pipeline, beating a field of bidders understood to have included AGL Ltd, Epic Energy, Borl Ltd and Alinta Gas. Page 25.

As part of a plan to expand its operations in Asia, Kerry Packer's paging offshoot Matrix Telecommunications is attempting to raise A$100 million through a private placement of 36 million shares at A$2-a-share, and with a non-renounceable rights issue.
Comitments are due by tomorrow. Page 25.

Following a loss for the nine months to March and amid continuing difficult trading conditions in the video sell-through and rental markets, the Network Entertainment Group Ltd has slashed its profit forecast for the second time since its December listing conceding yesterday it will not make even its revised estimate of A$2 million earnings. Page 25.

In a move which follows discussions last week between QuikTrak Networks Ltd and NRMA Ltd and an out of court settlement of a dispute about advertising claims, the two companies are again embroiled in a legal dispute, with QuikTrak seeking injunctions agaist NRMA, claiming the roadside service and insurance giant has not made full disclosure about its StarTrak vehicle location system. Page 27.
THE AUSTRALIAN

In a move which could have repercussions for Australia's Foster's Brewing Group Ltd, which is an equal partner with Grand Metropolitan Plc in the Inntrepreneur Pub Co Ltd, Grand Met and fellow British drink company Guinness Plc have stunned financial markts by announcing a A$41.67 billion merger to create a food and beverages giant incorporating a portfolio of the world's best-known brands. Page 21.

According to accounting firm KPMG's annual Financial Institutions banking industry survey, more fee increases are inevitable as banks face the end of an era of profit growth fed by generous margins on home lending. The survey reveals the four big banks have lost more than A$3 billion in revenue from significant rate cuts resulting from increased competition in the home loan market. Page 21.

CSR managing director Geoff Kells admitted yesterday the company's A$212 million net profit, which was down 34 per cent on 1995-96 and resulted in CSR slashing its dividend from 15 cents to nine cents a share, was not good enough, but said the company is inning its hopes on a profit rebound next year on cost cutting and a modest improvement in the housing market. Page 21.

As part of David Jones managing director Peter Wilkinson's bid to lift the upmarket retailer out of a sales and profit slump that the company admits is partly its own fault, he has scrapped plans for the company's first overseas outlet - in New Zealand - to focus on improving sales at its existing department stores. Page 21.

According to an article in the Wall Street Journal yesterday, EchoStar Communications Corp filed a broad breach of contract suit against The News Corporation Ltd in a Federal Court in Denver on Friday, alleging the media giant failed to meet the terms of A$2.6 billion satellite TV venture between the two companies. Page 23.

Federal Communications Minister Richard Alston has given the strongest indication yet the Government will not force CanWest Global Communications Inc to lessen its stake in the Ten Group Ltd to below 57.5 per cent, saying on Friday he did not believe the Canadian media group would be forced to divest its economic interest in Ten below its current level. Page 23
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

CSR managing director Geoff Kells has blamed a 12 per cent fall in housing starts and strong pressure on product prices for a 34 per cent fall in annual profit to A$212.2 million - the lowest profit result since 1993. The poor result was at the lower end of stockbroking analyst forecasts and CSR shares closed one cent lower at A$4.76. Page 25.

According to the KPMG Financial Institutions Performance Survey, issued yesterday, Australia's major banks have lost up to A$2 billion since the beginning of 1996 due to intense competition in the home lending market, and the banks have already started to try and compensate for the loss by increasing fees on banking transactions and credit cards. Page 25.

Amid continuing interest in Australia's oil and gas sector, at least A$100 million of new oil and gas floats are in the pipeline, aimed at broadening the scope for investing in the national energy sector. The first project is expected to be a A$20 million raising by newly-formed Australian World-Wide Exploration. Page 25.

The Federal Government plans to slash the number of tax jurisdictions that are deemed to be "comparable tax countries" from 61 to just seven, thus imposing a much tighter system on business, in today's Budget. The crackdown on international profit shiftin will impose a hefty burden on business, but the Australian Taxation Office believes that several hundred million dollars a year is being lost. Page 27.

After lengthy debates and a suite of amendments negotiated by the Democrats, the Federal Government's central revenue-raising measure in last year's budget - the 15 percent superannuation surcharge on high-income earners - has finally passed the Senate. The Government was forced to admit that the surcharge is a tax, with the amendments aimed at protecting low and middle-income earners from being taxed inadvertently. Page 27.

Network Entertainment has again revised downwards its full-year earnings forecasts for the second time in less than four months. The company will not meet its revised earnings forecast of $2.05 million after suffering a loss in the nine months to the end of March. Network Entertainment shares fell four cents to 30 cents. Page 27.
THE AGE

CSR has warned that its three Australian businesses of building and construction, materials, and timber face limited growth prospects and stiff prices pressure as the company yesterday posted a 36 per cent drop in full-year profits to A$212.2 million amida slump in the construction industry. Page B1.

According to the KPMG Financial Institutions Performance Survey, the net effect of intense competition in home lending for each of Australia's four big banks was up to A$500 million less profit from their home loan divisions since the beginning of last yer. Page B1.

In a deal which will reverse a slump in fur exports to eastern Europe over the past 10 years, the Adelaide Wool Company has won a contract worth up to A$150,000 to export 10,000 fox pelts this winter. The deal will see the company supply red fox furs to Poland and the Czech Republic. Page B1.

Freedom Furniture has moved against a slump in the retail market, with a seven per cent rise in sales from A$83.9 million to A$89.3 million contributing to an 84 per cent increase in net profit for the 26 weeks to March 30. The company has predicted that improved conditions will push earnings even higher in the coming months. Page B3.

Network Entertainment Group shares dropped by 12 per cent to a new low of 30 cents after it warned that it was unlikely to meet its annual earnings forecast of $2.05 million. The warning came just days after the unexplained departure of chairman Dr John Hewson, and only "small positive" earnings are now expected for the full year. Page B3.

A spokesman for New South Wales Treasurer and Energy Minister Michael Egan said yesterday the Government had an "open mind" about selling shares in Pacific Power. If the Government can convince the ALP, unions and caucus of the sale's merits it could be aproved, for more than $2 billion, by mid-year. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
